title: What a reader does with the browser
description: Each thing a reader sets out to do, step by step, with what happens when it goes another way.

entities.name: Open a repository and find a folder
entities.description: A reader gives an address and reaches the folder they want to read.
entities.goal: See a repository's views and knowledge, folder by folder.
preconditions: The page is open in a browser that can reach the repository's host.
postconditions: A folder is shown, and the address names it, so it can be shared or bookmarked.

flow.action: Gives the address of a GitHub or GitLab repository, a branch, tag or commit, or a folder, on the landing page; or opens a link that carries one.
Splits the address into the host, the repository, the ref and the folder.
Lists the repository's files at the ref. If the root has a .cyberspace-explorer folder it keeps that folder's .json files under the folder; otherwise it keeps the .dev/*.json files under the folder.
Reads every file, twelve at a time, keeps the ones whose kind it knows and sorts each folder's files by kind.
Shows the folder tree and the folder the address names, or the shallowest folder, with its first kind of view open.
Narrows the tree by typing part of a folder's name, a view's title, or the name or ID of something in it.
Opens a folder from the tree, from the chips under Inside, or from the crumbs above its name.
Opens the tab for the kind of view they want; the same kind stays open as they move between folders that have it.

alternatives.condition: The address is not http or https, or names no repository.
alternatives.outcome: The landing page stays, and the status line says what is wrong with the address.

alternatives.condition: The host refuses, or has no such repository or ref.
alternatives.outcome: The status line says why, and offers what could help: on the Worker, for a GitHub repository, Sign in with GitHub or Include private repositories; otherwise Add a token.

alternatives.condition: No .dev/*.json file (or .cyberspace-explorer/*.json file, where the root has that folder) is under the folder.
alternatives.outcome: The status line says so, and that the skills describe how to add them.

alternatives.condition: GitHub cuts the tree short because the repository is too large.
alternatives.outcome: The folders found are shown, and the status line warns that some may be missing.

alternatives.condition: A file can't be read, or is of a kind the page doesn't know.
alternatives.outcome: It is left out, and the status line names it and why.

alternatives.condition: The drawing library doesn't load.
alternatives.outcome: Every view is shown as its tables, and the status line says so.

entities.name: Add a token for a private repository
entities.description: A reader gives the browser their own access token so it can read a repository the host does not show to everyone.
entities.goal: Read a private repository, or one behind GitHub's hourly limit.
preconditions: The reader has an access token that can read the repository: on GitHub, fine-grained with Contents: read; on GitLab, with read_api.
The repository is not on GitHub, or the page is not served by a Worker that signs readers in; there, a GitHub refusal offers sign-in instead (sign-in-with-github).
postconditions: The token is kept in this tab, or in this browser if they asked, under the scope they chose.
Every request to that host carries it; no request to any other host does.

flow.action: Says why the host refused, and puts Add a token after the message.
Opens the token panel from that button, or from the Tokens button in the bar.
Pastes the token, chooses what it is for (every repository on the host, everything under an owner or group, or only this repository) and whether to keep it after the tab closes.
Keeps the token under that scope, replacing any other for it, and reloads.
Sends the token with every request to the repository's host, choosing the narrowest scope that covers the repository.

alternatives.condition: Nothing is pasted.
alternatives.outcome: Save closes the panel and nothing changes.

alternatives.condition: The browser won't store anything.
alternatives.outcome: The status line says the token can't be kept, so it can't be used.

alternatives.condition: The host refuses the token.
alternatives.outcome: The status line names the scope whose token was refused and says it may be wrong, expired or for another account, and offers Replace or add a token.

alternatives.condition: The token is for another account that can't see this repository.
alternatives.outcome: The status line suggests adding a narrower token for it.

entities.name: Sign in with GitHub and open my repository
entities.description: A reader signs in with GitHub on cyberspace-explorer.com and opens one of their own repositories, private ones included.
entities.goal: Read their own repositories, private ones included, without making or pasting a token.
preconditions: The page is served by its Worker with sign-in set up (/auth/me says configured).
The reader has a GitHub account.
postconditions: The Worker holds a session for the reader in a sealed cookie, for 7 days, and the page never sees their token.
The repository chosen is open, read through the Worker.

flow.action: Asks the Worker who is signed in, and shows Sign in with GitHub (optional) with a box to include private repositories.
Ticks include my private repositories if they want them, and presses Sign in with GitHub.
Authorizes the app at GitHub, where the Worker has sent them.
Comes back to the landing page signed in: it says who they are and fills the address box's drop-down with their repositories.
Types part of a name to narrow the list and picks a repository.
Opens it, listing and reading GitHub through the Worker.

alternatives.condition: The reader cancels at GitHub.
alternatives.outcome: The landing page says GitHub sign-in was cancelled.

alternatives.condition: The sign-in can't be finished: the state doesn't match, it took more than 10 minutes, or GitHub gives no token.
alternatives.outcome: The landing page says GitHub sign-in didn't work, and offers it again.

alternatives.condition: The repository is private and the reader signed in without private repositories.
alternatives.outcome: The status line says GitHub can't see it with this sign-in, and offers Include private repositories.

alternatives.condition: GitHub no longer accepts the reader's token.
alternatives.outcome: The Worker ends the session, and the status line asks them to sign in again.

alternatives.condition: The page is not served by the Worker, or its sign-in is not set up.
alternatives.outcome: Sign in with GitHub opens a field for a personal access token instead, kept in this browser for github.com.

entities.name: Find out about a part of a drawing
entities.description: A reader learns what one part of a diagram, use case or journey is, what it touches, and where it leads.
entities.goal: Understand a part and move to what is around or inside it.
preconditions: A folder with a drawn view is open on that view's tab.
postconditions: The part's inspector is open, or the folder it stands for is.

flow.action: Points at a part or a line.
Lights the part and its neighbours, fades the rest, and shows a tooltip saying what it is and what a click will do.
Clicks the part, or presses Enter or Space on it.
Pins the part and opens the inspector with everything the view says about it, its neighbours as links.
Follows a neighbour in the inspector, or a row in the tables under the drawing.
Brings that part into view, pins it and pulses it.

alternatives.condition: The part has a round badge: it stands for a folder with views of its own.
alternatives.outcome: The part grows into the page and that folder opens.

alternatives.condition: The drawing is larger than its frame and the reader drags it.
alternatives.outcome: It pans; the click that ends the drag selects nothing.

alternatives.condition: The reader presses Escape, the close button or the empty drawing.
alternatives.outcome: The inspector closes and the drawing rests.

entities.name: Read a folder's knowledge and follow a link
entities.description: A reader reads the knowledge files of a folder and follows a record's link to another.
entities.goal: Read what a folder knows about itself, and what it points to.
preconditions: The folder has at least one knowledge file.
postconditions: The record linked to is in view.

flow.action: Opens the Knowledge tab.
Shows the files grouped as the catalogue groups them, and each record as a card: title, status and evidence badges, ID, summary, details, its own fields, origin, relationships, sources and links.
Follows a relationship or a link in the details to another knowledge file.
Opens that folder on its Knowledge tab, scrolls to the record and flashes it.

alternatives.condition: The path is not a .dev file the page read, nor a folder it shows.
alternatives.outcome: It opens on the repository's host in a new tab.

alternatives.condition: The record the link names isn't in the file.
alternatives.outcome: The link goes to the file, and the missing ID is shown after it.

alternatives.condition: The path is a view, not a knowledge file.
alternatives.outcome: That view's tab opens, scrolled to it.

entities.name: See what is waiting
entities.description: A reader looks at every open decision and blocker in the repository at once.
entities.goal: Know what waits on whom, and what it holds up.
preconditions: The repository has a decision with status open, or a blocker that is not resolved, done, closed, removed, unblocked or cancelled.
postconditions: The record the reader chose is shown in its folder.

flow.action: Shows Waiting above the tree, with how many records wait.
Opens Waiting.
Shows two tables: open decisions (folder, who it waits on, what it blocks, context) and blockers (folder, who can unblock it, what it blocks, when it is unblocked).
Opens a record from either table.

alternatives.condition: Nothing is waiting.
alternatives.outcome: There is no Waiting link.

entities.name: Walk to a part and read it
entities.description: A reader in Cyberspace goes down from a city to eye level by one of its parts, walks among the parts round it, and reads them.
entities.goal: See a part from where it stands, with what it depends on in front of them, and read it and its neighbours.
preconditions: A city of a drawn view stands in Cyberspace (#<folder>|view:<file>|~space:city, or a part's focus with it).
postconditions: The part the reader chose is selected and its inspector open; the address names it in the street, and Esc takes them back up to the city.

flow.action: Selects a part of the city.
Lights its beams and opens the inspector, with Walk to <name> at its foot.
Presses Walk to <name>.

Flies the eye down to 1.7 units above the ground, 12 units from the part across the layout's flow, looking up at it, and puts the breadcrumb, the key hints, the map and a crosshair where the legend and camera controls were.
Walks with W A S D, looks by dragging, rises with Space, or clicks the map.
Moves the eye at the same pace whatever the frame rate, sliding along towers and stepping onto plates, and keeps the map, the breadcrumb and the status line saying where it is.
Points at a part nearby.
Shows the hover card beside its top: its name, what it does and how many beams it has.
Clicks a part, or presses Enter on the one under the crosshair.
Selects it and opens the inspector with what Flat says about it.

alternatives.condition: Nothing is selected, and the reader presses Walk in the camera controls.
alternatives.outcome: The eye goes down by the middle of the city.

alternatives.condition: The reader opens a street address directly.
alternatives.outcome: The city stands and the eye is put there at once.

alternatives.condition: The place 12 units out is inside a tower.
alternatives.outcome: The eye stands a unit further out at a time until it is clear.

alternatives.condition: The reader prefers reduced motion.
alternatives.outcome: The eye is put there at once; walking still moves, because the reader drives it.

alternatives.condition: The reader presses Esc.
alternatives.outcome: The selection clears; pressed again, the eye rises back to the city's orbit, and once more to the folder's tower.
